title: How Language Models Organize Moral Knowledge
hook: Six moral foundations, six linear probes: the directions neither collapse into one 'morality detector' nor sit independently — they span near-maximal dimensions while sharing a common component.
key_points: Trains six independent linear probes on open-weight models, one per Moral Foundations Theory category.
The learned directions span a near-maximal number of independent dimensions while sharing a positive common component.
That shared component is moral-specific: mean pairwise cosine 0.26 versus 0.013 for a matched non-moral concept battery.
The geometry is consistent across architectures and scale, and reaches its integration regime early in pretraining — before probe accuracy saturates.
No evidence of the individualizing/binding split predicted by Moral Foundations Theory; structure reflects corpus statistics instead (an underpowered test — only 20 candidate partitions).
Most of a dilemma's variance encodes conflict-specific structure: the model represents moral tension, not a pre-resolved judgment.
content_html: Detecting that text is about morality is a low bar; models clear it easily. Reblitz-Richardson asks the harder question: do LLMs distinguish moral foundations from one another, and is there geometric structure in how they relate?
extra_html:
The setup

Six independent linear probes are trained on open-weight models, one per Moral Foundations Theory category — care/harm, fair/cheat, liberty/oppression, loyalty/betrayal, authority/subversion, sanctity/degradation — and the resulting directions are compared in representation space.

Two null results were plausible: the directions could collapse into a single moral detector, or sit fully independent. Neither happens. They span a near-maximal number of independent dimensions while sharing a positive common component. That shared component is the signature of integration, and it is moral-specific — mean pairwise cosine 0.26, against 0.013 for a matched non-moral concept battery built the same way. The geometry holds across architectures and scales, and arrives early in pretraining, well before probe accuracy saturates.

What it doesn't find

No evidence of the individualizing/binding distinction that Moral Foundations Theory predicts; the structure looks more like corpus statistics. The author flags this as an underpowered test — only 20 candidate partitions exist.

Dilemmas

Extending to moral dilemmas, each dilemma direction partially composes from its component foundations, at 2.7x a mismatched-pair baseline. But the majority of its variance encodes conflict-specific structure. The reading the paper offers: the model represents moral tension itself rather than a pre-resolved judgment — which is a more interesting object for alignment work than a scalar "how moral is this" signal.

related.title: Circuit Condensation: Train the Circuit Smaller
related.hook: Circuit discovery on a frozen model returns hundreds of edges nobody can check. Post-train the model to route the behavior through fewer, and circuits shrink 8x on average — up to 316x.

related.title: Constitutional AI
related.hook: What if a model could critique and improve its own answers against a written set of principles, instead of relying on humans to label every harmful case?

flashcards.prompt: What would it have meant if the six moral probe directions had collapsed into one?
flashcards.back_html: That the model has a single undifferentiated morality detector — able to flag moral content but not to distinguish care from fairness from loyalty. They don't collapse.

flashcards.prompt: What does the paper conclude about how models represent moral dilemmas?

Dilemmas are represented as a weighted average of the winning foundation
Dilemmas have no distinguishable representation from single-foundation content

flashcards.explanation_html: Dilemma directions partially compose from their component foundations at 2.7x a mismatched-pair baseline, but the majority of variance is specific to the conflict itself.

flashcards.prompt: How do we know the shared component across moral directions is moral-specific?
flashcards.back_html: A matched non-moral concept battery, built identically, has mean pairwise cosine 0.013 versus 0.26 for the moral directions.
